snippet.title: Humans Picked a Fight With a Volcano · 11.ai
snippet.description:
Humans tried to stop lava three times: with bombs, with explosives and with the ocean. 🌋

🇺🇸 1935, Hawaii: lava from Mauna Loa was heading for Hilo. On 27 December the US Army Air Corps bombed the flow, in an operation planned by then-Lt. Col. George S. Patton. Six days later the lava stopped, but volcanologists still argue whether the bombs did anything.
🇮🇹 1992, Italy: Etna's lava climbed right over the earth walls built to protect Zafferana Etnea. So engineers blasted its lava tube near the source, and only one building was lost.
🇮🇸 1973, Iceland: on 23 January the ground ripped open on Heimaey, an island of 5,300 people. Within six hours almost everyone was on the mainland. Then for five months crews pumped about 7.3 billion liters (7.3 million m³) of seawater onto the lava. It stopped about 100 m short of closing the harbor, and the new rock made the harbor even better.

Final score: Humans 2, Volcano 0*
*Hawaii: it's complicated.

Which method would you have tried? 👇

Sources: USGS (Hawaiian Volcano Observatory "Volcano Watch", SIM 2932-A, OF 97-724, "Man Against Volcano"), Wikipedia (Mauna Loa, Mount Etna, Eldfell).

snippet.title: Australia Lost to 24 Rabbits · 11.ai
snippet.description:
Christmas Day 1859: a ship brought 24 rabbits to Australia — family records say only 13 got on. By 1950 there were an estimated 600 million. Australia fought back three times: a £25,000 prize (Louis Pasteur entered with chicken cholera), a rabbit-proof fence from ocean to ocean that the rabbits beat before it was finished, and a virus that escaped its island quarantine, most likely on flies. Final score: Rabbits 2, Flies 1, Australia 0. Today there are still an estimated 200 million.

Sources: CSIRO · National Museum of Australia · State Library of Western Australia · Alves et al. 2022, PNAS · Government of Western Australia, 18 Oct 1996.

Credits: Voice — ElevenLabs (elevenlabs.io). Music — "Frame-Dragging", The Grey Room / Density & Time (YouTube Audio Library). Fence line — Historic Number 1 Rabbit Proof Fence (DPIRD-046), Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development WA, CC BY 4.0, simplified. Maps — Natural Earth. Photos — Louis Pasteur by Paul Nadar; Rabbit-Proof Fence No. 1, 1926, State Library of WA (public domain). 3D models — Kenney (CC0).

snippet.title: The Longest Traffic Jam in History: 8 YEARS  · 11.ai
snippet.description:
14 ships went into the Suez Canal for a one-day trip. They got out 8 years later.

June 1967: a convoy of cargo ships was inside the canal when the Six-Day War broke out. Egypt sank ships to block the canal, and 14 of them were stuck in the Great Bitter Lake, right on the front line, for almost eight years. Desert sandstorms dusted them yellow, so they became the Yellow Fleet.

The ships came from 8 countries on both sides of the Cold War. Their sailors, about 3,000 of them taking turns over the years, became friends: football on deck, their own stamps, even their own Olympics in 1968. Poland won.

In May 1975 only two ships, the West German Münsterland and Nordwind, could sail home on their own. Tens of thousands welcomed them in Hamburg. Part of the cargo: kitchen clocks. Delivered only eight years late.

The Ever Given blocked the Suez Canal for 6 days in 2021. These ships waited 8 years.

How many stars would you give this delivery? ⭐

Sources: Capt. Bryan Hill, "Postage Stamps of the Great Bitter Lake Association" (1975) · American Shipper, Aug 1975 (Hapag-Lloyd account, reprinted by FreightWaves) · Der Spiegel (2008, captains' accounts) · mare No. 40 (2003) · Wikipedia: Yellow Fleet.

Credits
Voice: ElevenLabs (11.ai)
Music: "Frame-Dragging" by The Grey Room / Density & Time (YouTube Audio Library)
Maps: made with Natural Earth (public domain)
3D: made in Blender with Kenney assets (CC0) and Poly Haven textures and HDRI (CC0)
Animation, sound effects and Atlas: The Atlas Ape

snippet.title: USA vs BRITISH EMPIRE… Over ONE Pig
snippet.description:
The Pig War, 1859: America and Britain almost went to war over ONE pig 

June 1859, San Juan Island: American farmer Lyman Cutlar caught a pig eating his potatoes — and shot it. The pig belonged to Charles Griffin of the British Hudson's Bay Company. Cutlar offered $10. Griffin wanted $100.

Both countries claimed the island, so it escalated fast: 461 American soldiers with 14 cannons against five Royal Navy warships with 70 guns and 2,140 men. Governor James Douglas wanted the Americans gone — but Rear Admiral Robert Baynes refused to start a war "over a squabble about a pig".

So both sides just stayed. For 12 years. They even partied together on national holidays. In 1872, German Emperor Wilhelm I's arbitration gave the islands to the United States.

Total casualties: one pig.
Bonus: US park rangers still raise the British flag at English Camp on San Juan Island every single day 

Team farmer or team pig ? Tell me below

Sources: Wikipedia "Pig War (1859)" · HistoryLink.org essay 5724 (after Michael Vouri, "The Pig War: Standoff at Griffin Bay", 1999) · San Juan Island National Historical Park (NPS)

Credits
Animation & host: The Atlas Ape
Voice: ElevenLabs
Music: "Frame-Dragging" by The Grey Room / Density & Time (YouTube Audio Library)
Map elevation: AWS Terrain Tiles (Mapzen / Tilezen — SRTM, USGS 3DEP, GMTED2010, ETOPO1, CDEM)
Flags: Wikimedia Commons (public domain)

snippet.title: He Sold Everything to Meet Her
snippet.description:
He sold everything and rode a bus 2,000+ km across Brazil to meet the farm widow he followed online. Nobody there had ever seen her…

He says he'll go back to the same place. Should he?

The story: in October 2026 a 49-year-old bricklayer from Imperatriz (Maranhão) travelled to Belo Horizonte to meet "Jéssica Fazendeira", a farm widow with 300,000+ followers. A local radio station told him the truth: she was an AI-generated character. Her anonymous creator says the account was made to sell products. Back home, he said he would try again.
Reported by Rádio Itatiaia, TV Mirante, g1, UOL and Dexerto.

Pictures: AI illustrations of fictional characters (Google Flow) — not the real people. City photos: Wikimedia Commons — Imperatriz sign by Hernandezjean80 (CC BY-SA 4.0), Belo Horizonte bus terminal by Tet (CC0), Belo Horizonte skyline by Spicypepper999 (CC0). Map: Natural Earth. Meme clips (Confused Travolta, Stonks, "here we go again") used as commentary / parody.
Music: "Frame-Dragging" — The Grey Room / Density & Time (YouTube Audio Library).

en.title: He Sold Everything to Meet Her
en.description:
He sold everything and rode a bus 2,000+ km across Brazil to meet the farm widow he followed online. Nobody there had ever seen her…

He says he'll go back to the same place. Should he?

The story: in October 2026 a 49-year-old bricklayer from Imperatriz (Maranhão) travelled to Belo Horizonte to meet "Jéssica Fazendeira", a farm widow with 300,000+ followers. A local radio station told him the truth: she was an AI-generated character. Her anonymous creator says the account was made to sell products. Back home, he said he would try again.
Reported by Rádio Itatiaia, TV Mirante, g1, UOL and Dexerto.

Pictures: AI illustrations of fictional characters (Google Flow) — not the real people. snippet.title: He Escaped Prison Dressed as a Doctor
snippet.description:
He escaped prison 4 times — and never broke a single lock. 
Steven Jay Russell: a police radio, a fake judge, a green marker… and one last trick nobody saw coming.

His story inspired the 2009 film "I Love You Phillip Morris" starring Jim Carrey.
